messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a prototype dashboard for continuous batching metrics. primary ask: a wait-vs-fill heatmap + batch-size distribution + node saturation lane. Can runtime/infra confirm signal availability?

ajay: We emit these already but split across services. Relevant metric names: `batch_enqueue_latency_ms` (histogram), `batch_fill_ratio` (gauge), `batch_size` (histogram, per-queue), `node_gpu_util_percent` (gauge).

sam: Who owns stitching these into panels? I can wire up the Grafana side if we get canonical promql and owners for each metric.

lina: Runtime owns `batch_*` metrics (that's me). Infra owns the node-level signals (zach). We should also decide cardinality for labels — queues can explode. Recommend `{queue=~"(api|dedicated|private)"}` tagging.

zach: Confirm infra side: `node_gpu_util_percent` and `node_mem_saturation` exist. They come from node-exporter + custom exporter for GPU. We can add `instance_role` label to correlate pool (e.g., serving, dedicated).

maria: Perfect. Two UX asks from console/product: (1) heatmap should be interactive by queue and model variant, (2) we want a saturation alert that triggers before latency SLOs break.

eva: For heatmap bins, suggest x-axis = wait_time_ms buckets, y-axis = batch_fill_percent (0-100), color = request count. We already have histograms but may need a derived metric `batch_wait_fill_count` from buckets if Grafana can't do join easily.

ajay: Alternative PromQL (rough):

```
# heatmap cell value = rate of requests in wait bucket & fill bucket
sum by (wait_bucket, fill_bucket) (increase(batch_enqueue_latency_ms_bucket[5m]))
```

This gets messy with two separate histograms. Might be easier to emit a combined 2D histogram proto from runtime — small change but simpler and cheaper in query time.

sam: Is emitting a 2D histogram feasible short-term? If not, we can approximate with a sampled export: every Nth batch emit `batch_wait_ms, batch_fill_pct` as a gauge with `wait_bucket`/`fill_bucket` labels.

lina: 2D histograms would be clean but require runtime changes. Sampling gauge approach is lower risk. We can ship sampling in 1 sprint. I'll open an RFC + PR.

zach: Alerting idea: define `saturation_margin = 100 - avg(node_gpu_util_percent)` per pool. Fire when `saturation_margin < 15` AND `p95(batch_enqueue_latency) > X`. Want to avoid noisy alerts, so combine both signals.

maria: Good. Product wants a dashboard panel that shows marginal risk score (0-100) computed from saturation + fill-rate drop + p95 wait. Can infra provide the node inputs as a single derived metric?

ajay: We can add a `pool_saturation_score` gauge from infra side that aggregates nodes per pool. Will need a small collector job.

dash-bot: dashboard/template created: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/waitfill-proto — contains placeholder panels for heatmap, batch-size histogram, and saturation lane.

sam: I'll fork and add the promql once we settle on the sample format. Can we add owners to each panel in the template? e.g., runtime = @lina, infra = @zach, console = @maria.

lina: Yes, I'll own the sampling-export PR and add the `wait_bucket` and `fill_bucket` labels. Target: end of next sprint (2 weeks).

zach: I'll spin up the collector for `pool_saturation_score` this week. ETA: 3 days.

maria: Timeline looks good. Action items:
- lina: RFC + sampling PR for `batch_wait_ms`/`batch_fill_pct` export (2w)
- zach: collector job for `pool_saturation_score` (3d)
- sam: wire Grafana panels and add owners to template (this sprint)
- ajay: provide example promql snippets and perf notes (today)

ajay: sharing quick perf notes: avoid `count()` over high-cardinality labels; prefer pre-aggregated `pool_saturation_score` and sampled gauges. Also keep query windows >= 5m to smooth noise.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone hits blockers ping here. I'll schedule a 30m sync mid-sprint to review prototype. :calendar: :thumbsup:

zach: ack.

lina: ack, starting RFC now.

sam: ack, will update the template after ajay posts snippets.

maria: Closing thread for now — will reopen with sync invite.
